title: ⚖️ Discussion Essays (Discuss both views)

sections.heading: The key difference
sections.body:
"Discuss both views and give your own opinion" = you must:
1. Discuss View A fairly and objectively
2. Discuss View B fairly and objectively
3. Give YOUR OWN clear opinion

A common Band 5–6 mistake: writing body paragraphs that only support one view and ignoring the requirement to "discuss both".

sections.heading: Structure option A (balanced)
sections.body:
Introduction: Outline both views + state your position
Body 1: Those who believe [View A] argue that... [evidence]
Body 2: On the other hand, advocates of [View B] contend that... [evidence]
Conclusion: Restate your overall position

highlight: "Discuss both views" does NOT mean "agree with both equally." You must still give YOUR position clearly in the introduction and conclusion.

sentence: Urban farming requires significant investment. _______, the long-term environmental benefits may outweigh the initial costs.
explanation:
"Nevertheless" is perfect here — it says "even though there's a problem (high cost), the result (benefits) still stands."

It's stronger and more academic than "However" alone. Use it when you want to say "this difficulty exists, BUT the main point remains valid."
hint: The sentence first gives a problem, then says the benefits still matter — that's a contrast/concession.

instruction: Match each essay element to its purpose:

pairs.meaning: State the main idea of each body paragraph
Explain and provide evidence for your point

explanation:
A well-structured essay shows the examiner you can organise information logically — this directly boosts your Coherence & Cohesion score.

Band 9 essays have CLEAR topic sentences at the start of every body paragraph. Examiners can read just the first sentence of each paragraph and understand the entire argument.

question: A Task 2 question says: 'Discuss both views and give your own opinion.' You only discuss one view. What mark will this affect MOST?
explanation:
'Discuss BOTH views' is a direct instruction. Ignoring one view = failure to complete the task = Task Response penalty.

Task Response assesses:
• Did you address ALL parts of the question?
• Did you present a clear position?
• Are ideas fully developed?

Missing a sub-task is the most common high-band student error.

question: Which discussion essay introduction is Band 8?
options: 'This essay will discuss both views about technology.'
'Some people like technology and some people don\'t. I will discuss this.'

'The question of whether technological advancement represents a net benefit to humanity has generated considerable debate, with proponents emphasising enhanced productivity while critics point to growing social fragmentation.'
'Technology has advantages and disadvantages and I will explain them in this essay.'
correct: 'The question of whether technological advancement represents a net benefit to humanity has generated considerable debate, with proponents emphasising enhanced productivity while critics point to growing social fragmentation.'
explanation:
✅ 'The question of whether...' = nominalized structure (Band 8+)
✅ 'has generated considerable debate' = impersonal academic framing
✅ 'proponents emphasising... critics point to' = identifies BOTH sides concisely
✅ 'net benefit' and 'social fragmentation' = precise, sophisticated vocabulary
✅ No 'I will discuss' announcement

question: Where in a discussion essay should you state YOUR OWN opinion?
options: Never — just present both views fairly
explanation:
For 'Discuss both views AND give your own opinion' questions:

✅ Introduction: 'While I acknowledge both perspectives, I believe...'
✅ Body 1: Present View A (fairly)
✅ Body 2: Present View B (fairly)
✅ Conclusion: Restate YOUR position clearly

Your opinion must appear in BOTH intro and conclusion for Task Response marks.

❌ 'Only in conclusion' = late position = weaker Task Response score
❌ 'Never' = fails to 'give your own opinion' = Task Response penalty
